headline: Red Sox enjoying a quiet intermission before the Rays visit Fenway
morning_brew: Not much action on the field today, which puts me in mind of that wild afternoon back in two-thousand-and-four when Dave Roberts swiped second base. I was posted up at a bar in Southie, and the place had basically cleared out after the seventh inning like everyone had somewhere better to be. I was just about to follow suit and head out into the night, but then Roberts took off, and the entire room erupted in a way I have never heard since. Watching that game unfold was like staring into the abyss, only to have it blink back at you and decide that maybe, just maybe, it was our turn to hold the cards.

That night in Southie taught me that you never walk out on a game until the final out is recorded, no matter how hopeless things look. We spent the rest of the evening high-fiving strangers and acting like we had just witnessed the end of the world, which in a way, we had. It is the kind of local legend status that keeps me glued to the tube every single night, even when the box scores are not giving us much to cheer about. You sit through the slow stretches because you know exactly how sweet the payoff tastes when the stars finally align.

The squad has a brief window to regroup before the Rays head into the Hub for a series starting tomorrow. I am planning to keep things low-key around the house, maybe get some chores done if I can muster the motivation, but mostly I am just waiting to see if we can maintain the pace. I have been spending way too much time staring at the standings lately, so stepping back for a minute is probably for the best. I will be ready to go once the first pitch is thrown at the park tomorrow.

When he is hitting his spots like this, the opposing hitters might as well be swinging at shadows.
